content:
Kieran Culkin weighed in on a “Succession” spinoff, and it’s clear he has some very strong feelings about it.

The actor appeared on the U.K.’s “Heart Breakfast” radio show last week, and spoke to hosts Amanda Holden and Jamie Theakston about his new movie, “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.”

Holden couldn’t help but sneak in a question about “Succession,” the hit HBO series that ran from 2018 to 2023.

“I know we’re not here to talk about this, but I’m still grieving the end of ‘Succession,’” Holden said.

“Oh, you are? Get over it! It’s been three years!” Culkin said, sounding an awful like the character he portrayed on the show, Roman Roy.

Culkin had a similarly cheeky answer when asked about the idea of a show spinoff.

“I think that would be a terrible idea,” he said. “I mean, what are you hoping for? ‘Cousin Greg: The Sitcom?’”

Culkin spoke about filming with showrunner and creator Jesse Armstrong, who he says “spent the entire last season trying to figure out if there was a way to do one more.”

“I never wanted to know what was going to happen in the season, and on the fourth one I did ask,” the actor said. “When he pitched me the end of the season, and I went ‘Well, that kind of sounds like it’s the end of the show.’ And he goes, ‘It’s the end of the show.’ And he went, ‘But...’ and of the top of his head, pitched me like three different ideas of what Season 5 could be, they all sounded good.”

Despite the possibilities, Culkin said the show “ended perfectly” and “the way it was supposed to.”

But according to an interview with The New Yorker, Armstrong isn’t entirely ruling out a future spinoff or prequel.

“The feeling that there could be something else in an allied world, or allied characters, or some of the same characters — that’s also strong in me,” he said back in 2023.

“Maybe there’s another part of this world we could come back to, if there was an appetite?” he said. “Maybe there’s something else that could be done, that harnessed what’s been good about the way we’ve worked on this. So that is another true feeling.”
